environment: Windows 11 Pro x64, MSVC 19.51, GNS 1.6.1 and OpenSSL 3.6.5 via vcpkg 65a2c23, loopback; real time
game_exe_sha256: N/A (prototype does not touch the game)
objective: Implement ChatGPT review #10 (FB-10-01..05 and answer 5) on feature/ki35-ki37-investigation: EventAck bounded by sent ids, events marked sent only on Sent, stateless DTLS cookie gate, explicit leave handshake (protocol v3), KI-35 instrumentation, soak gate v6; investigate KI-35 and KI-37 from traces before any tuning.
hypothesis: Per-attempt traces from both processes show where the secure reconnect time and the lost GNS leave go; mechanisms found are fixed in code, not by tuning; gate v6 (fixed before its runs) is met by all 12 soaks.
procedure: Implemented FB-10-01/02 with tests; stateless DTLSv1_listen cookie gate; protocol v3 DisconnectAck with client Leaving state; dtls_trace records (content type/epoch/handshake type per record, timers, milestones; no secrets) plus clock records mapping logs onto the shared steady clock; tools/soak/timeline.py; gate v6 (p5 RTT floor with 100 samples, per-client delivery, leave_confirmed, distributions) documented before its runs. 8 quick 30 s harsh secure soaks traced (4 UDP, 4 GNS), mechanisms fixed, 8 more after the fix, then the full battery: 12 x 120 s v6 soaks, all suites x2 on both builds, E2E, asymmetric x4, secure E2E x4, KI-27 reproducer x20.
expected_result: All tests pass; the traces identify the KI-35 and KI-37 mechanisms; all 12 soaks pass gate v6.
observed_result: Mechanisms found from the traces and fixed: (1) OpenSSL retransmits a DTLS flight one datagram per record (5 per flight), so a round only succeeded if all 5 survived; one quick harsh UDP run needed 9 client timers and 6.3 s of handshake. Flights are now coalesced up to the MTU; regression test: 2 retransmission rounds -> 2 datagrams (was 10). (2) After the transport came up the client waited up to the 500 ms reconnect retry before its ConnectRequest; it now sends at once. (3) KI-37 on GNS: the host closed the connection right after acking the leave, and the close notice overtook the delayed unreliable DisconnectAcks (2 of 4 quick harsh-gns-secure runs failed leave_confirmed); the host now keeps the transport peer open 1.5 s. (4) Found by the FB-8-01 test after the coalescing change: the global ClientHello rate limit before the cookie gate let forgeries starve a real player's cookie-bearing ClientHello (8.3 s, test failed); cookie-proven ClientHellos now bypass the budget (243 ms). Full battery: 11 of 12 v6 soaks passed 59/59, including harsh-gns plaintext (failed in v5, KI-37); harsh-gns-secure failed client2_recovery_time at 4168 ms (v5: 3358). Its trace: about 1 s waiting for the host timeout notice, 2.5 s of cookie exchange and handshake with the first two ClientHellos lost (hypothesis KI-38: sent before the GNS connection was established), 0.7 s of ConnectRequest retry. harsh-udp-secure recovery 1397 ms (v5: 1810). All suites passed twice on both builds; E2E, asymmetric 4/4 and secure E2E 4/4 passed. KI-27 reproducer: 16-63 assertions per run with no settle (10/10 runs), 0 with the 50 ms settle (10/10 runs). Quick 30 s runs fail realized_rtt_floor by design (fewer than 100 RTT samples). One lan-udp run (094607) was aborted when its battery was restarted outside the tool time limit; kept, with no summary. Independent review (agent) after the battery found and we fixed: non-expiring cookies that bypassed every budget (now 30 s slots, separate proven budget), spoofed floods denying every first ClientHello (reserved 20/s per established address), events overtaking a refused or backing-off one (FB-10-02 test: 41 client gaps before, 0 after), unbounded and unauthenticated repeated DisconnectAcks (now only peers in their leave window, 1 per 100 ms), an unbounded client leave loop. After the fixes: UDP-build suites passed x2; GNS build passed except GNS-backed timing checks (3 transport-contract tests on unchanged GNS code; GNS case of one DTLS no-busy-loop check, DTLS 50/51), KI-39: the suites had depended on another program holding 1 ms timer resolution (Sleep(1) measured 16 ms). timeBeginPeriod alone helped only in visible-console launches, because Windows 11 ignores it for windowless processes (ctest children, hidden launches); the runner now also opts out of that throttling (GNS case 199 -> 2010 iterations under a hidden launch; transport contract passes under ctest). test.ps1 also used to skip copying GNS results on a failing ctest (stale evidence); fixed. Final suite results are in the tests-*.json logs of this run. Secure E2E 2/2; soaks harsh-udp-secure 59/59 (1467 ms) and moderate-gns-secure 59/59 after the fixes. Final recorded suite pass after all fixes (two passes run; the logs hold the last): dtls 51/51, integration 44, integration-gns 30 + 14 skipped, network 17, network-gns 12 + 5 skipped, transport 18, transport-both 20, unit 17, gns 7; all passed.
errors: harsh-gns-secure soak failed the 3 s recovery gate (KI-35 on GNS); KI-38 unverified; one aborted run kept; the GNS case of the flight-coalescing test is NOT RUN (process-global impairment). KI-39 (test timing vs system timer resolution) found and fixed during verification.
follow_up: KI-38: log the inner GNS Connected time and decide whether DTLS should start only after it; characterise the harsh-gns-secure recovery distribution over several 120 s runs; durable events (KI-28b); LAN test; independent review.
